newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mixed, rate concerns linger.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mixed, rate concerns linger.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed on Monday as lingering concerns about a possible Bank of Canada rate hike kept activity muted and discouraged buyers from entering the market, dealers said.

"The rumors abounding about a hike, I think that caused a little bit of the uncertainty in the market and that caused the real backup. I think you don't really have nibbling here, you have people just sort of watching," said one T-bill trader with a Canadian bank.
Canada's three-month cash T-bill firmed to yield 3.34 percent from 3.35 percent at Friday's close.

Canadian T-bills opened weaker on Thursday and Friday as recent signs of a stronger economy, combined with weakness in the currency, spurred speculation of a near-term Bank of Canada rate hike. The Bank of Canada last month surprised market by hiking rates 25 basis points, its first tightening in more than two years.

Some dealers cautioned that the money market was trying to lead the Bank of Canada into a tightening, just as it led the central bank in easing rates last year. However, this time conditions are different and dealers said it is unlikely the market could force the bank to tighten.

"They are keeping a watchful eye on things, but I don't think that there's enough information to hike yet," the trader said. "I think we're probably close to the tops (in yields) for right now without a hike."
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.72 percent from a 3.71 percent on Friday. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 4.20 percent from 4.21 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.25 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
